speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're a child with a 3-week history of fatigue, fever, easy bruising, and severe leg pain. To better understand what might be happening, can you describe the pain in your legs more specifically—is it worse at night or when you move?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing generalized fatigue and easy bruising for 3 weeks. Over the past week, she has developed a fever and severe leg pain that wakes her up at night.

speaker: Doctor
text: The nocturnal nature of the leg pain is very concerning for bone involvement. Have you noticed any specific lumps, swelling, or warmth in your legs, and does anyone at home see you complaining of bone pain? Also, has there been any recent bruising on your arms or trunk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and easy bruising. I also have Fever, Severe leg pain that disturbs sleep. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) with possible pathological fractures or bone marrow expansion.

The "cellulitis" diagnosis was likely incorrect given the systemic symptoms and nocturnal bone pain; we need to confirm this immediately. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and peripheral blood smear. REQUEST TEST: Bone Marrow Biopsy. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of lower extremities.
